A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Explicit Logic Channel study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and supplementary Sections A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 11 MLLMs on NegBench, HC-RefCOCOg and HC-RefLoCo, including accuracy, consistency, fusion results and supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original error audits, joint-outcome analyses, component ablations, fusion diagnostics and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The extraction, grounding, logical reasoning, consistency calculation and aligned-fusion procedures are retained. Equation (5) is rewritten into an algebraically equivalent normalization-and-rescaling form. SAM3 and oracle substitutions are experimental variants, not revisions to the proposed core method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MC-VQA and HC-REC coverage: NegBench COCO/VOC2007, HC-RefCOCOg and HC-RefLoCo. The added analyses reuse these datasets; the manually annotated subset and oracle controls do not introduce a new task or population.

E2.justification: The original 11 MLLM comparators remain. Supplementary Table 12 adds SAM3 alongside GroundingDINO in a component comparison, and main Table 1 newly includes an ELC-only VOC2007 comparison. Most other ELC-only rows added to the main tables already appeared in v1's supplement.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols are retained. New protocols include manually auditing consistent-but-incorrect cases at IoU 0.5, testing 100 randomly selected HC-RefCOCOg validation samples with manually supplied nouns and boxes, and measuring component latency. These are additional evaluations, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's model-choice ablations and inconsistent-example studies, v2 adds systematic analyses of incorrect agreement, joint channel outcomes, error propagation through noun extraction and grounding, prediction changes caused by fusion, and latency. Supplementary Sections B.2–B.3 and D.3–D.5 substantially expand scrutiny of reliability and component behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The existing correlation and fitted-trend analyses remain unchanged. New error-category percentages and confusion matrices summarize outcomes rather than introduce uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation results are retained, but v2 adds substantial diagnostic results. Examples include reported incorrect-agreement rates of 0.0437 and 0.0473, and ELC Acc50 of 0.82 with GroundingDINO versus 0.98 with oracle boxes on the new 100-sample study. Fusion-change counts and latency results are also new. These are additional findings under specified conditions, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(13) are substantively unchanged; Equation (5) is algebraically equivalent. The added empirical outcome categories and explanatory rationale do not introduce a new theorem, proof, derivation or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain unchanged. The introduction and Section 4.2 add a limited extension: changes made by fusion can help verify the relative reliability of the two channels without ground-truth labels, beyond improving predictions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses incorrect agreement as a risk to CR-based trust, attributing audited cases to shared model bias, ELC errors and annotation problems. It also interprets oracle ablations as exposing upstream error propagation and fusion changes as reliability cues. These qualify and extend the retained interpretation rather than replace it.

D1.justification: Supplementary Table 14 newly reports component execution times and the models used for those measurements, improving visibility into computational cost. The existing prompts, dataset-access instructions and two-RTX2080Ti hardware disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Handbook of Logic in Artificial Intelligence and Logic Programming, Logic in Computer Science, and TFAR. These support task adaptation and training-free reliability positioning; the related-work discussion and broader differentiation from prior methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with localized rewriting around aligned fusion and an added task-adaptation paragraph. Supplementary Section B is reorganized into B.1–B.3, Section C is retitled, and D.3–D.5 are appended. This is an extension rather than extensive rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds five supplementary tables and a three-example incorrect-agreement figure, redraws main Figure 1 to show aligned fusion separately, and adds ELC rows to main Tables 1–3. Other diagrams, plots and case-study images are retained, with relocation or renumbering and limited layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new error audits, oracle ablations and latency reporting address gaps in v1. However, added supplementary Table 2 has HC-RefCOCOg outcome percentages totaling only 89.7–89.9%, and its discussion attributes InternVL3.0 results to Qwen3.0. These unresolved reporting errors weaken the new reliability evidence. With the original method and primary results retained, the diagnostic benefits and accuracy concerns do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
